title: Command injection through system()
root_cause: The host string is concatenated into a shell command line and handed to system(), which runs it through /bin/sh. Shell metacharacters in the input (like ';') are interpreted by the shell, not treated as literal text.
defenses: Avoid system() and popen() on any data that is not a fixed, trusted string.
Use the exec-family calls (execve, execlp, ...) with an explicit argument array -- there is no shell to interpret metacharacters.
Validate with an allow-list of acceptable characters before using external input at all.
Run with least privilege, so a successful injection still has little to reach.
